mainTopic: Impurity inside the body: a יולדת whose baby's head has left the פרוזדור, and whether hidden places count as בלוע or בית הסתרים.
overview: This amud first finishes a discussion of רבי זירא's ruling about a woman who went to the מקוה before blood left her body. רבי ירמיה shows that her case is not like someone who swallowed a נבלת עוף טהור. So רבי זירא must mean the blood actually came out after her טבילה. Her טבילה does not protect her from that blood. The גמרא then explains why a ברייתא lists a יולדת separately: the baby's head has left the פרוזדור, so it counts as born even while still inside. A story with רבא shows the practical result for a ברית on שבת. Next, אביי and רבא argue whether a woman's inner place, and the throat where a bird נבלה makes one טמא, count as בלוע (fully swallowed) or בית הסתרים (a hidden part of the body). Each side brings a proof, and the proofs are discussed. Finally רבא rules on a שרץ or a נבלה caught in a body fold, and on bringing such a שרץ into an oven. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The swallowed bird comparison does not fit blood
steps.stepSummary: Swallowing a נבלת עוף טהור is a kind of טומאה that only exists inside the body. Blood is normally טמא once it comes outside, so it should be treated that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the swallowed bird has no impurity outside the body. Here, blood should simply make her impure when it comes outside.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה, continuing his challenge to רבי זירא, shows that comparing a woman's blood to someone who swallowed a נבלת עוף טהור does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נבלת עוף טהור only makes a person טמא when it is swallowed; touching it outside does nothing. Blood is different, because it makes a person טמא once it is outside the body. So there is no reason to give blood a special inside-the-body טומאה like the bird has.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity that works outside the body, through ordinary contact
Outside (Aramaic)
Let it make impure
There / here, the standard way of setting two cases side by side

steps.confusionAlert: The 'there' case is the swallowed נבלת עוף טהור from the earlier discussion. The 'here' case is the woman's blood. Do not mix the two up.

phrases.english: There, it has no impurity outside;
phrases.notes: 'There' means the swallowed carcass of a kosher bird, which only makes you impure once it is in your throat.

phrases.english: here, when it goes outside, let it make her impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי ירמיה's objection to רבי זירא, which began on the previous amud. He shows that the possible comparison to a swallowed נבלת עוף טהור does not work.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of a woman's blood to a swallowed נבלת עוף טהור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bird has only inside-the-body טומאה. Blood has ordinary outside טומאה, so it should only make her טמא once it comes out.

steps.title: רבי זירא means the blood came out after her טבילה
steps.stepSummary: Because of that difficulty, רבי זירא's case must be talking about blood that actually left her body after she went to the מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is talking about a case where the blood came outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads רבי זירא's ruling a new way: she is טמאה only because the blood came out after her טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The swallowed-bird idea is dropped. The woman is not טמאה because of blood sitting inside her. She is טמאה because that blood later came outside, where blood is normally טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too
When it came outside

phrases.english: Here too, it is when it came out outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the difficulty in step 1 by redefining רבי זירא's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי זירא's woman was טמאה from blood still inside her, like the swallowed bird.
steps.terutzMaskana: She is טמאה only because the blood came outside after her טבילה.

steps.title: Then why did רבי זירא need to say it?
steps.stepSummary: If the blood came outside, it obviously makes her טמאה, so the ruling seems unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the blood came outside, what is the point of saying this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading: blood that leaves the body is plainly טמא, so why teach it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows blood outside the body is טמא. If that is all רבי זירא meant, his statement seems to add nothing. The גמרא needs to find the new point he is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? This is obvious, so why teach it?

phrases.english: If it came out outside —
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading given in step 2 as making the ruling obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבי זירא spoke of blood that came outside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood outside the body is clearly טמא, so the ruling would teach nothing new.

steps.title: Her טבילה does not protect her from blood that comes out later
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought her טבילה also covers blood that was inside her at the time it took place. רבי זירא teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since the immersion works for the blood that was inside her, it should also work for this blood. So he teaches us that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי זירא is blocking a mistaken idea: that her טבילה covers any blood that was inside her when she went in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her טבילה does help in one way: blood that stays inside her does not make her טמאה. We might have stretched that and said the טבילה also covers blood that was inside then and came out later. רבי זירא teaches that blood which comes out after the טבילה still makes her טמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said, which introduces a mistaken idea the ruling comes to block
Since, used when we extend a rule from one case to a related one
Immersion in a מקוה to become טהור
Inside (Aramaic)
It teaches us, the new point of the ruling

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא's ruling: a woman who went to the מקוה becomes טמאה again if blood leaves her body afterward, even though that blood was already inside her during the טבילה.

phrases.english: You might have said:
since immersion is effective
for blood that is inside,
let it also be effective for this blood —
phrases.notes: 'This blood' means the blood that was inside during the טבילה and only came out afterward.

phrases.english: so he teaches us that it is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by naming the mistake רבי זירא's ruling prevents.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing what is new in the ruling (מהו דתימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the טבילה works for blood that stays inside, it should also cover blood that was inside then and came out later.
steps.terutzMaskana: Blood that comes out after the טבילה still makes her טמאה.

steps.title: Back to the problem with the ברייתא about a יולדת
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא is now explained, but the ברייתא that lists a יולדת separately still makes no sense, since her blood is already נדה or זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our teaching is resolved, but what about the woman after childbirth? If the blood comes in her days of נדה, she is a נדה. If it comes in her days of זיבה, it is זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the original question about the ברייתא, which is still open now that רבי זירא is explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the new reading, רבי זירא holds blood only makes her טמאה once it comes out. So his ruling cannot explain why the ברייתא lists a יולדת as טמאה from the inside. Her blood is already covered by the listings of נדה or זבה, so the separate listing still needs a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Our teaching, here meaning רבי זירא's ruling
Was resolved, its difficulty was answered
A woman who has given birth
Days when blood makes her a נדה
Days when blood makes her a זבה

phrases.english: Our teaching has been resolved,
but what about a woman after childbirth?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the ברייתא that lists a יולדת among things that make her impure even while still inside.

phrases.english: If it is in her days of menstruation, she is a menstruating woman;
if it is in her days of ziva, it is ziva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the רבי זירא side discussion and goes back to the earlier question on the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's separate listing of a יולדת as מטמא בפנים כבחוץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A יולדת's blood already falls under נדה or זבה, which the ברייתא lists separately. So listing her again seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The ברייתא means a birth with no blood
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a dry birth, where no blood came out, and teaches that she is still טמאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A dry birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא lists the יולדת because of a birth with no blood at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no blood came out, she cannot be טמאה as a נדה or a זבה. The birth itself makes her טמאה. That explains why the יולדת gets her own place in the list.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? This sets up a narrower case
A dry birth, with no blood coming out

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
With a dry birth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by limiting the ברייתא to a birth without blood.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about the blood of a יולדת, which would just be נדה or זיבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a dry birth, where the birth itself makes her טמאה.

steps.title: In a dry birth, what is impure inside?
steps.stepSummary: If there is no blood at all, nothing is 'impure inside as outside,' so the dry-birth answer does not fit the ברייתא's wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: A dry birth? What is there that makes impure inside as it does outside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the dry-birth answer, because it does not fit the category the ברייתא is listing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists things that make a person טמא while still inside the body, just as they would outside. In a dry birth there is no blood, so there is nothing inside that counts as טמא. The answer explains why she is טמאה, but not why she belongs in this list.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes impure inside just as outside, the heading of the ברייתא's list
There is

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying a dry birth fails to make her טמאה. The problem is only that a dry birth does not fit the ברייתא's heading of something impure while still inside.

phrases.english: A dry birth?
What is there that makes impure inside as it does outside?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵידָה יַבִּשְׁתָּא מַאי מְטַמֵּא בִּפְנִים כְּבַחוּץ אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the ברייתא refers to a dry birth
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's list is about things that are טמא while still inside the body. A dry birth has no blood inside, so it does not belong on that list.

steps.title: The baby's head has left the corridor
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a baby whose head came out past the פרוזדור. It counts as born even though it is still inside, as רב אושעיא also holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, where the baby put its head out past the corridor. This fits רב אושעיא, who said: it is a decree, in case the baby put its head out past the corridor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 7. 'Impure inside as outside' means a baby whose head has left the פרוזדור. It is still inside the mother, but it already counts as born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 asked how a dry birth could be called 'inside as outside.' The answer is that the word 'inside' refers to the baby, not to blood. Once its head is past the פרוזדור it counts as born, so the mother is a יולדת and טמאה. רב אושעיא is brought because his decree is built on the same idea.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'corridor', the inner passage the baby goes through before it comes fully out
Put out its head. Once the head is past the פרוזדור, the baby counts as born
A baby or newborn
A protective rule made by the חכמים

steps.whatToRemember: A baby whose head has left the פרוזדור counts as born, even though it is still inside the mother.

phrases.english: For example, where the baby put out its head
outside the corridor,
phrases.notes: The baby is still inside the mother, but past this inner passage. That is why the ברייתא can say 'inside as outside.'

phrases.english: and this is like Rav Oshaya,
for Rav Oshaya said:
It is a decree, in case the baby put out its head
outside the corridor.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהוֹצִיא וָלָד רֹאשׁוֹ חוּץ לַפְּרוֹזְדוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 by changing what 'inside' refers to: the baby, not blood.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'inside as outside' had to be about blood, which does not fit a dry birth.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about a baby whose head left the פרוזדור. It is still inside but counts as born, so the mother is a טמאה יולדת.

steps.title: A man asks רבא about a ברית on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A man asks רבא whether one may do a ברית on שבת. רבא says yes, then realizes the question must hide something, so he goes back to ask what really happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like the man who came to רבא and asked: May one circumcise on שבת? רבא said: It is fine. After he left, רבא said: Could that man really not know that a ברית is allowed on שבת? He went after him and said: Tell me, my friend, what actually happened?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that shows the same idea in real life. Here the story is only being set up. The key ruling comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows that a ברית on the eighth day pushes aside שבת. So רבא understands the man must have had a special case. This sets up the facts that make the 'head out of the corridor' rule matter.

keyTerms.meaning: To circumcise, to do a ברית מילה
It is fine, it is allowed
Could you imagine? Used to show something is hard to believe
The actual facts of the case

phrases.english: And this is like that man who came
before Rava,
He said to him: May one circumcise on Shabbat?
He said to him: It is fine.
After he left, Rava said:
Could you imagine that this man
did not know that it is allowed to circumcise on Shabbat?!
He went after him and said to him:
Tell me, my friend,
how did the actual incident happen?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a story that shows the step 8 idea, that a head past the corridor counts as born.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The man asks whether a ברית may be done on שבת. רבא then asks for the real facts behind the question.

steps.title: The baby counted as born on Friday, so no ברית on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The baby was heard crying on Friday before שבת but was born on שבת. רבא rules it counted as born on Friday, so a ברית on the next שבת would be on the wrong day and does not push aside שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The man said: I heard the baby cry toward evening on Friday, but it was not born until שבת. רבא said: This baby put its head out past the corridor. So a ברית on שבת would not be at its proper time, and any ברית not at its proper time does not push aside שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא hears the facts and rules. The baby was heard crying before שבת, so its head was already out. It counts as born on Friday, and its ברית may not be done on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the baby was heard on Friday, its head must have been past the פרוזדור, so its birth counts from Friday. Its eighth day is then the next Friday, not שבת. A ברית on the wrong day does not push aside שבת. This shows in practice that a head past the corridor counts as birth.

keyTerms.meaning: Cried out, made a sound
Toward evening on ערב שבת, just before שבת
A ברית done not on its proper day, the eighth day
Doing work that is forbidden on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: A head past the פרוזדור counts as birth. This sets the eighth day for a ברית, and a ברית on the wrong day does not push aside שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: The baby really came out fully on שבת, but its birth is counted from Friday, when its head came past the corridor. That is why its eighth day is not שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the 'head out of the corridor' rule has real practical results, here for when a ברית may be done on שבת.

phrases.english: He said to him: I heard the baby
cry out toward evening on Friday,
but it was not born until Shabbat.
He said to him: This one put out its head
outside the corridor,
and so it is a circumcision not at its proper time,
and any circumcision not at its proper time
we do not break Shabbat for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שְׁמַעִית וָלָד דְּצָוֵיץ אַפַּנְיָא דְּמַעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the facts and רבא's ruling, completing the story begun in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That a baby whose head is past the פרוזדור counts as born.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling that a baby heard crying before שבת counts as born on Friday, so its ברית is not on שבת.

steps.title: Is the inner place of a woman hidden deep inside, or just a concealed part?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: should the inner place of a woman be treated as בלוע, fully inside the body, or as בית הסתרים, a hidden part of the body?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: That place of a woman, is it considered 'swallowed' inside the body, or is it a hidden part of the body?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the inner place of a woman. Which category of 'inside' does it belong to? Here the question is only being asked. The answer comes later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two categories have different rules for טומאה. Something בלוע, fully inside the body, is treated differently from something in a בית הסתרים, a hidden fold. The גמרא wants to know which category this place falls into.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the חכמים, an open question
'That place', a polite way to refer to a woman's private area
'Swallowed', something fully hidden inside the body
A hidden part of the body, like a fold, which is not fully inside

phrases.english: They asked:
That place of a woman,
is it considered 'swallowed' inside,
or is it a hidden part of the body?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: אוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם שֶׁל אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the story with רבא ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the inner place of a woman counts as בלוע or as בית הסתרים for the laws of טומאה.

steps.title: What difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between בלוע and בית הסתרים. It answers with a case: a friend placed a כזית of נבלה inside a woman's body. If the place is בלוע, she stays טהור. If it is בית הסתרים, she becomes טמא through משא (carrying).
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference? Suppose her friend pushed an olive-sized piece of a dead animal into that place. If you say that place counts as 'swallowed' inside the body, then swallowed impurity does not make anyone impure. But if you say it is a hidden part of the body, then even though she does not become impure by touching it, she at least becomes impure by carrying it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why the question from the last step really matters. It gives a case where the two answers lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the inner place is בלוע, the נבלה counts as completely swallowed, and swallowed טומאה does nothing at all. If the inner place is only בית הסתרים, touching there does not count as מגע. But she is still carrying the נבלה, and משא makes her טמא anyway. So the answer decides whether she is טמא or טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?
An olive-sized amount, the smallest amount of נבלה that makes something impure
The body of an animal that died without proper שחיטה; it is a source of טומאה
Impurity that is fully swallowed inside a body; it does not make anyone impure
Becoming impure by touching
Becoming impure by carrying or lifting, even without touching

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ways of becoming impure. בית הסתרים only blocks מגע (touching). It does not block משא (carrying). בלוע blocks everything.

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?
For example, where her friend inserted into her
an olive-bulk of a dead animal into that place.
phrases.notes: 'That place' means the inner place of the woman, the place the question from the last step was about.

phrases.english: If you say it counts as swallowed,
swallowed impurity does not make impure.
But if you say it counts as a hidden part of the body,
granted that she does not become impure by touching,
she at least becomes impure by carrying!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the practical result of the question asked in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference there is between calling the inner place בלוע or בית הסתרים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With a כזית of נבלה inside her: if it is בלוע she is טהור; if it is בית הסתרים she is טמא through משא.

steps.title: אביי and רבא disagree
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the inner place is בלוע. רבא says it is בית הסתרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It counts as swallowed. רבא said: It counts as a hidden part of the body.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite answers to the question. This sets up the proof and the answer that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, the woman in the נבלה case stays טהור, because swallowed טומאה does nothing. According to רבא, she becomes טמא through משא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is / it counts as
It counts as swallowed (אביי's view)
It counts as a hidden part of the body (רבא's view)

phrases.english: אביי said: It counts as swallowed.
רבא said: It counts as a hidden part of the body.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: בָּלוּעַ הָוֵי, רָבָא אָמַר: בֵּית הַסְּתָרִים הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two opinions on the question that step 12 showed has a practical difference.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: the inner place is בלוע. רבא: it is בית הסתרים.

steps.title: רבא's proof from a ברייתא about semen
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא. It says a woman becomes טמא from semen inside her only because of a special גזירת הכתוב, since this is טומאת בית הסתרים, which normally does not make one impure. So the inner place is בית הסתרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How do I know this? Because a ברייתא teaches: 'It is only because it is impurity in a hidden part of the body, and impurity in a hidden part of the body does not make impure. Rather, it is a decree of the Torah.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a source to support his view. The ברייתא calls semen inside the woman 'טומאת בית הסתרים'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא explains why the Torah needed to teach that a woman becomes טמא from semen inside her. Its reason is that the semen is in a בית הסתרים. If the ברייתא labels that place as בית הסתרים, then it is not בלוע, and that matches רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (introduces a proof)
Impurity in a hidden part of the body; normally it does not make one impure through touch
A decree of the Torah, a rule that comes straight from the פסוק and not from normal logic

phrases.english: רבא said: From where do I say this?

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: ״אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁטּוּמְאַת בֵּית הַסְּתָרִים הִיא״.
phrases.english: As it is taught: 'It is only because it is impurity in a hidden part of the body,'
phrases.notes: This ברייתא is about a woman becoming טמא from semen inside her body (ויקרא 15:18). Only its key line is quoted here.

phrases.english: and impurity in a hidden part of the body does not make impure,
but it is a decree of the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא supports his opinion from step 13.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that the inner place is בית הסתרים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that calls semen inside a woman 'טומאת בית הסתרים'.

steps.title: אביי: the ברייתא gives two reasons
steps.stepSummary: אביי reads the ברייתא as giving two separate reasons. First, it is בלוע. Second, even if you call it בית הסתרים, it still would not make one impure. So the ברייתא does not prove that the place is בית הסתרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי? He says the ברייתא is saying one thing and then adding another. One: it is swallowed impurity. And another: even if you want to say it is impurity in a hidden part of the body, it still does not make impure. Rather, it is a decree of the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how אביי answers רבא's proof. He reads the ברייתא in a way that fits his own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא took the ברייתא's words 'טומאת בית הסתרים' as its real view of the place. אביי says the ברייתא's main reason is that it is בלוע. The בית הסתרים line is just an extra 'even if you say so' argument. Either way, the woman should be טהור, which is why the Torah needed a גזירת הכתוב.

keyTerms.meaning: He is saying one reason and then adding another
Even if you were to say (an extra, fallback argument)
It does not make impure

steps.whatToRemember: אביי says the inner place is בלוע, and רבא says it is בית הסתרים. רבא's proof from the ברייתא is answered by אביי: the ברייתא gives two reasons ('חדא ועוד'). Its main reason is בלוע, and בית הסתרים is only a backup argument.

phrases.english: And אביי? He says it is saying one reason and another:
One, that it is swallowed impurity;
and another, even if you want to say
that it is impurity in a hidden part of the body,
it still does not make impure,
but it is a decree of the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof from step 14 by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא, not רבא's view itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא assumed the ברייתא's 'בית הסתרים' was its actual view of the place. It may be only a secondary 'even if you say' argument after the main reason of בלוע.

steps.title: Is the throat-place of a bird carcass swallowed or hidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the place in the throat where נבלת עוף טהור makes a person טמא counts as בלוע or as בית הסתרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: the place where a kosher bird's carcass makes a person impure (the throat). Is it considered swallowed, or is it considered a hidden part of the body?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question, built just like the earlier question about a woman. Now it asks about the throat, where a bird carcass makes a person טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נבלת עוף טהור does not make a person טמא by touching or carrying it. It only makes him טמא while it is in his throat as he eats it. So the גמרא asks how to define that spot: is food there already 'swallowed' (בלוע), or is it still in a 'hidden place' (בית הסתרים)?

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before the חכמים (an open question)
The carcass of a kosher bird that was not properly slaughtered
Swallowed, fully inside the body
A hidden part of the body, not visible but not fully swallowed

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same question as before. Earlier the question was about a woman's inner place. Now it is about the throat. The two questions are built the same way, which is why the גמרא repeats the pattern.

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
The place of the carcass of a kosher bird —
phrases.notes: He means the throat. That is the only place where a bird carcass makes a person impure.

phrases.english: is it considered swallowed,
or is it considered a hidden part of the body?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel question to step 11, now applied to the throat instead of a woman's inner place.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the throat-place of נבלת עוף טהור has the status of בלוע or of בית הסתרים.

steps.title: The practical difference: a piece of animal carcass stuck in someone's mouth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows why the question matters. Someone's friend stuck a כזית of animal נבלה into his mouth. If the throat is בלוע, he stays טהור. If it is בית הסתרים, he becomes טמא through משא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make? Take a case where a person's friend stuck an olive-size piece of animal carcass into his mouth. If you say the throat counts as swallowed, swallowed impurity does not make anyone impure. But if you say it is a hidden part of the body, then even though he is not impure by touching it, he is at least impure by carrying it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical difference the question makes, and answers with a case of animal נבלה placed in a person's mouth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal נבלה normally makes a person טמא by touch (מגע) and by carrying (משא). Touching inside a בית הסתרים does not count, but carrying does. So if the throat is only בית הסתרים, the person still 'carries' the נבלה and becomes טמא. If it is בלוע, the impurity is completely swallowed and he stays טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference?
Stuck or pushed in
An olive-size amount, the minimum size for many laws
Swallowed impurity, which does not make a person impure
Becoming impure by touching
Becoming impure by carrying

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?
For example, where his friend stuck
an olive-size piece of carcass into his mouth.
If you say it is considered swallowed —
swallowed impurity does not make impure;
but if you say
phrases.notes: Some versions read the words in round brackets; the corrected wording is the one in square brackets, 'and if.'

phrases.english: it is considered a hidden part of the body —
granted that by touching he does not become impure,
by carrying, at least, he becomes impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the question in step 16 matters, just as step 12 did for the earlier question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference there is between calling the throat בלוע and calling it בית הסתרים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כזית of animal נבלה placed in the mouth: if בלוע, the person stays טהור; if בית הסתרים, he is טמא through משא.

steps.title: אביי says swallowed, רבא says hidden
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that the throat is בלוע. רבא rules that it is בית הסתרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it is considered swallowed. רבא said: it is considered a hidden part of the body.
steps.whatsHappening: The two אמוראים take opposite sides on the question, just as they did about the woman's inner place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, a person with animal נבלה stuck in his throat stays טהור. According to רבא, he becomes טמא through carrying it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is (considered)
It is considered swallowed (אביי's view)
It is considered a hidden part of the body (רבא's view)

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is considered swallowed,
and Rava said: It is considered a hidden part of the body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two answers to the question raised in steps 16-17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: the throat-place is בלוע. רבא: it is בית הסתרים.

steps.title: אביי proves his view from a ברייתא about an animal carcass in the throat
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא. It teaches that an animal נבלה does not make clothes טמא while it is in the throat, because the פסוק about becoming טמא through eating applies only to something whose whole impurity comes through eating, meaning the bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: How do I know this? A ברייתא teaches: You might think an animal carcass makes clothes impure while it is in the throat. So the verse says: 'A carcass or a torn animal he shall not eat, to become impure through it.' This is about something whose only impurity comes from eating it. That leaves out this animal carcass, which is already impure before he eats it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a source to support his view that the throat counts as בלוע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the פסוק about becoming טמא by eating is only about the bird, whose impurity comes only through eating. An animal נבלה, which is already טמא by touch and carrying, does not make a person טמא while it is in the throat. אביי reads this as proof: if the throat were only בית הסתרים, the animal נבלה there should still make him טמא by carrying, so the throat must be בלוע.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I know this? (introduces a proof)
One might have thought
Therefore the verse teaches
The carcass of an animal (not a bird)
The throat, the place of swallowing
An animal that was torn or fatally injured

steps.whatToRemember: A bird נבלה makes a person טמא only in the throat. An animal נבלה does not make a person טמא in the throat at all. אביי uses this to say the throat counts as בלוע.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is אביי's support for his side of the parallel מחלוקת, and it sets up the next question: can רבא explain this ברייתא his own way?

phrases.english: Abaye said: From where do I say this?
As it is taught in a baraita:
One might think that an animal carcass
makes clothes impure while it is in the throat?
Therefore the verse says:
"A carcass or a torn animal he shall not eat,
to become impure through it."

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאֵין לָהּ טוּמְאָה אֶלָּא אֲכִילָתָהּ —
phrases.english: This is about something that has no impurity except through eating it —
phrases.notes: That is the kosher bird, which is impure only while being swallowed.

phrases.english: this one is left out,
since it is already impure before he eats it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's position from step 18 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that the throat-place counts as בלוע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא 22:8 teaching that animal נבלה does not make clothes טמא while it is in the throat, since the eating-impurity applies only to something impure solely by eating.

steps.title: A logical argument that animal נבלה should make one impure in the throat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא with a קל וחומר. A bird נבלה is weaker, since touching or carrying it does not make you טמא, yet it makes you טמא when it is in your throat. An animal נבלה is stronger, since touching and carrying it do make you טמא, so surely it should also make you טמא in the throat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn it with a קל וחומר from a kosher bird's נבלה. A kosher bird's נבלה has no impurity outside, yet it has impurity inside. So this animal נבלה, which does have impurity outside, should surely have impurity inside too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's rule that an animal נבלה does not make clothes טמא while it is in the throat. It uses a קל וחומר, a 'how much more so' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Outside' means touching or carrying the נבלה. 'Inside' means having it in your throat while swallowing. A bird נבלה has only the inside kind of impurity, while an animal נבלה has the outside kind. So logic says the stronger animal נבלה should have the inside kind as well.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'how much more so' argument: if the weaker case has a rule, the stronger case should surely have it too
Impurity from outside the body, meaning from touching or carrying
Impurity from inside the body, meaning while the item is in the throat
A kosher bird that died without proper slaughter

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of impurity. Everyone agrees that carrying an animal נבלה makes you טמא. The argument here is only about the special impurity that comes from having it in your throat.

phrases.aramaic: וְתֵיתֵי בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר מִנִּבְלַת עוֹף טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: And let it come through a kal vachomer from the carcass of a kosher bird:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the rule that an animal נבלה makes you טמא while it is in your throat.

phrases.english: If the carcass of a kosher bird,
which has no impurity outside,
phrases.notes: Touching or carrying a bird נבלה does not make you טמא.

phrases.english: has impurity inside,
then this one, which does have impurity outside,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ טוּמְאָה בִּפְנִים?
phrases.english: is it not logical that it has impurity inside?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתֵיתֵי בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר מִנִּבְלַת עוֹף טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule in the ברייתא quoted in step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that an animal נבלה does not make clothes טמא while it is in the throat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from the weaker bird נבלה, which does make you טמא in the throat, to the stronger animal נבלה

steps.title: The word בָּהּ limits throat impurity to the bird
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says בָּהּ, 'through it'. This teaches that impurity in the throat comes only through the bird נבלה and not through any other נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'through it'. That means through it and not through another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קל וחומר by pointing to one word in the פסוק that limits the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר is only logic, and a word in the פסוק that limits a rule overrides that logic. The word בָּהּ marks throat impurity as something special to the bird נבלה. So the animal נבלה does not get it, even though it is stronger in other ways.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Through it and not through another.' A word that limits a rule to one specific case

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a limiting word in a פסוק can block a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: The verse says: "through it"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:8, the פסוק about נבלה making a person טמא through eating, which is understood to be about the bird.

phrases.english: through it, and not through another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר from step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: A limiting word in the פסוק overrides the logical argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: By logic, the animal נבלה should make you טמא in the throat, just like the bird does
steps.terutzMaskana: The word בָּהּ limits throat impurity to the bird נבלה only

steps.title: Then what does וְהָאוֹכֵל teach about animal נבלה?
steps.stepSummary: If eating an animal נבלה does not make you טמא, the גמרא asks why the פסוק about animal נבלה says 'and one who eats'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say 'and one who eats'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 21. A פסוק about animal נבלה mentions eating, so that פסוק seems to say that eating it does make you טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא 11:40 says that one who eats from an animal נבלה must wash his clothes. That sounds like eating an animal נבלה makes clothes טמא, which contradicts what we just learned from בָּהּ. So the גמרא needs to explain what the word וְהָאוֹכֵל is doing there.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so.' This introduces a problem that follows from the answer just given
'What does the פסוק come to teach?' This asks why a word is written in the פסוק
'And one who eats.' A word in the פסוק about animal נבלה

phrases.english: If so,
why does the verse say "and one who eats"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 21 using another פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only the bird נבלה makes one טמא through eating
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק about animal נבלה mentions eating, which suggests that eating it does make one טמא

steps.title: וְהָאוֹכֵל sets a כזית size for touching and carrying
steps.stepSummary: The word וְהָאוֹכֵל does not create impurity through eating an animal נבלה. It gives the size needed for touching and carrying: just as eating is measured by a כזית, so are touching and carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to give a size for one who touches and one who carries, the same as for eating. Just as eating is with a כזית, so too touching and carrying are with a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the word 'one who eats' is there to teach a size. It does not teach a new kind of impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions eating only as a measuring stick. Eating is always measured by a כזית, so touching or carrying an animal נבלה also needs a כזית to make you טמא. This way the word וְהָאוֹכֵל has a job, and the limit from בָּהּ still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: A required minimum size
One who touches
One who carries
The size of an olive, the standard size for eating

steps.whatToRemember: An animal נבלה does not make clothes טמא while it is in the throat, because the word בָּהּ limits that impurity to the bird נבלה. The word וְהָאוֹכֵל only teaches that touching and carrying an animal נבלה require a כזית. This supports אביי, whose ברייתא this is.

phrases.english: It comes to give a measure for one who touches and one who carries,
like one who eats:
just as eating is with an olive-size,
so too touching and carrying are with an olive-size.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word in the פסוק a different job: it sets a size
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word וְהָאוֹכֵל teaches that eating an animal נבלה makes one טמא
steps.terutzMaskana: The word וְהָאוֹכֵל sets a כזית as the size for touching and carrying an animal נבלה

steps.title: A שרץ versus a נבלה in a body fold
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a שרץ in a person's body fold leaves him טהור, while a נבלה in his body fold makes him טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: if a dead creeping creature is in the folds of a person's body, he is pure. If an animal carcass is in the folds of his body, he is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רבא comparing two kinds of impurity hidden in a fold of the body, like the armpit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both a שרץ and a נבלה make a person טמא when he touches them in a normal way. Yet רבא gives them opposite results when they sit in a hidden body fold. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead creeping creature from the eight listed in the תורה; it makes things טמא
His body fold, such as the armpit or a fold of skin
The carcass of an animal that died without proper שחיטה
Ritually pure / ritually impure

phrases.english: Rava says:
A creeping creature in his body fold — he is pure,
an animal carcass in his body fold — he is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of impurity in the throat to a new ruling about impurity in a hidden body fold.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שרץ in a body fold leaves the person טהור; a נבלה in a body fold makes him טמא.

steps.title: Why the שרץ leaves him pure and the נבלה makes him impure
steps.stepSummary: A שרץ makes things טמא only by touch, and a hidden body part cannot become טמא by touch. A נבלה also makes things טמא by carrying, so he is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A creeping creature in his body fold leaves him pure, because a creeping creature makes things impure only by touching, and a hidden part of the body cannot become impure by touching. An animal carcass in his body fold makes him impure, because even if it cannot make him impure by touching, it still makes him impure by carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind each half of רבא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is in how each one passes on impurity. A שרץ works only through מגע, and בית הסתרים does not count for מגע, so nothing happens. A נבלה also works through משא, and holding it in your body fold is carrying it, so he becomes טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Touching; one of the ways impurity passes on
A hidden part of the body, like an armpit or a fold of skin
Carrying; a נבלה makes a person טמא when he carries it, even without touching
Granted that; even if

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a נבלה is weaker or stronger by nature here. The only point is that a נבלה has an extra way of passing on impurity, carrying, which still works when touching does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that בית הסתרים does not become טמא by touch, which shapes the next case about bringing the שרץ into an oven.

phrases.english: A creeping creature in his body fold, he is pure —
it is through touching that a creeping creature makes impure,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הַסְּתָרִים לָאו בַּר מַגָּע הוּא.
phrases.english: and a hidden part of the body cannot become impure by touching.
An animal carcass in his body fold, he is impure —
granted that it does not make impure by touching,
by carrying, at least, it does make impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבא's two rulings in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שרץ passes on impurity only by touch, which does not apply to בית הסתרים; a נבלה also passes on impurity by carrying, which does apply.

steps.title: Bringing the שרץ in the body fold into an oven
steps.stepSummary: If a person with a שרץ in his body fold brings it into the air of an oven, the oven becomes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a creeping creature was in his body fold, and he brought it into the air space of an oven, the oven is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds another case about the same שרץ in a body fold: what happens when the person puts that part of his body inside a clay oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A clay vessel like an oven becomes טמא when a שרץ enters its air space, even without touching its walls. Here the שרץ enters the oven's air while still tucked in the person's fold, and רבא says the oven still becomes טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Air space; the empty inside of a vessel
An oven, made of earthenware, which becomes טמא through its air space
He brought it in

phrases.english: A creeping creature in his body fold,
and he brought it into the air space of the oven — it is impure.
phrases.notes: The one that becomes impure here is the oven, not the person.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁרֶץ בְּקוּמְּטוֹ, וְהִכְנִיסוֹ לַאֲוִיר הַתַּנּוּר — טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further ruling from רבא about the same case of a שרץ in a body fold, now affecting an oven.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שרץ in a body fold that is brought into the air of an oven makes the oven טמא.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to teach this, since a שרץ in an oven's air always makes it טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's second ruling as something we already know and did not need to be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows that a שרץ inside the air of a clay oven makes it טמא. So why should it matter that the שרץ happened to be in someone's body fold? The גמרא wants to know what new point רבא is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; the גמרא asks why a ruling even needs to be stated

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רבא's ruling in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the oven becomes טמא when the שרץ in the body fold is brought into it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שרץ in an oven's air space always makes the oven טמא, so the ruling seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: You might have thought: the פסוק says 'its inside'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain the new point: one might have thought that, since the פסוק says ״תוכו״, the rule applies only in a certain way.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since the Merciful One said 'its inside'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by describing a mistaken thought that רבא's ruling comes to correct. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about clay vessels says impurity comes when a שרץ falls into ״תוכו״, its inside. This word could make someone think the oven becomes טמא only when the שרץ itself falls inside, not when it is carried in inside a person's body fold. The גמרא will finish this thought next.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said; introduces a mistaken idea the ruling comes to reject
Its inside; the word in the פסוק about a שרץ falling into a clay vessel
The Merciful One; a name for ה׳ when the גמרא quotes the תורה

phrases.english: Lest you say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to answer the challenge of step 27 by showing why רבא's ruling is not obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows that the ruling rejects a reasonable mistaken reading of a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the פסוק says ״תוכו״, one might think the oven becomes טמא only when the שרץ itself falls inside it, and not when it is brought in tucked in a person's body fold.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling teaches that the oven does become טמא in this case. The full explanation continues on the next amud.
